The *Kusalakathā* ("Discourse on the Wholesome") is a debate text preserved within the nineteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 19.6) in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Like other debates in the collection, it investigates specific doctrinal propositions using dialectical cross-examination regarding what constitutes wholesome (*kusala*) states. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in a single language [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature passages surveyed address this chapter directly, mentioning *kusala* only as a general doctrinal and psychological concept across Buddhist literature.
According to DharmaNexus match analysis, the text exhibits extensive Pali-internal text reuse with 17 other texts in the canon, comprising 379 shared passages [DharmaNexus]. These recurring debate structures and formulaic interrogation sequences are shared predominantly with other chapters of the *Kathāvatthu*, most substantially with the *Rūpaṁkammantikathā* (Kv 8.9), *Rūpaṁmaggotikathā* (Kv 10.2), and *Rūpaṁkusalākusalantikathā* (Kv 16.7), alongside chapters addressing sense bases, results, and causes such as Kv 12.4, Kv 12.3, Kv 16.5, Kv 16.6, and Kv 16.8 [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches meeting significance thresholds are detected in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus].
